text:
Luke Evangelista's first season in New Jersey after 253 games in Nashville has a strange shape. The Devils are dominating with him on the ice: they get 60.7% of the expected goals at five on five when he plays, 5.3 points better than without him. And yet he has 11 points in 18 games, with just one goal and four points in his last ten.

The culprit is finishing around him. His line has scored 4.7 fewer goals than its chances deserve, and his own shooting sits at 8.3%. That usually swings back. Our range on his scoring rate runs from 2.0 to 2.8 points per 60, and he's at the low end.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among 401 forwards in wins above replacement, with strong numbers at both ends, though some of that came from hot shooting. He's a passer first, 89th percentile in primary shot assists in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. On a team that has won eight of ten, he's doing the work; the points are lagging behind it.
